text: The stroke of eleven: the signal shines out from the middle window
why: ¶219-220 state that at the stroke of eleven a single bright light shone from the middle window, which Holmes calls their signal.

text: The stroke of eleven: Holmes springs to his feet and says it is their signal, from the middle window
why: ¶220 states that Holmes springs to his feet, calls it their signal, and says it comes from the middle window.

text: Has Dr. Roylott really gone to rest when the signal shows?
why: Helen said Roylott retired early (¶35), and the lamp goes out at nine (¶219). Whether he is truly asleep is an open question the story gives reason to raise.

text: Has Dr. Roylott really gone to rest when the signal shows? — he has gone to bed for the night
id: q.roylott_at_eleven=he has gone to bed for the night
why: The light in the Manor went out about nine (¶219), and Helen's plan assumes he will retire for the night (¶184). Bed is a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: Has Dr. Roylott really gone to rest when the signal shows? — he has gone to his room but is still awake
id: q.roylott_at_eleven=he has gone to his room but is still awake
why: Helen's plan depends on hearing him retire (¶184), and the story gives no confirmation that he has actually slept, so being awake is a possibility a reader could weigh.

text: Does Dr. Roylott suspect that the room will be watched to-night?
why: Roylott has traced Helen and confronted Holmes (¶100-111), and Holmes says the old man knows they are looking into his affairs (¶115). Asking whether he suspects a watch is a fair question.

text: Does Dr. Roylott suspect that the room will be watched to-night? — he suspects nothing and goes about his night as usual
id: q.roylott_suspects=he suspects nothing and goes about his night as usual
why: Suspecting nothing is a plain possibility; the story has not ruled it out, though Roylott's confrontation makes it less likely.

text: Does Dr. Roylott suspect that the room will be watched to-night? — he has seen the lamp or otherwise knows of the watch
id: q.roylott_suspects=he has seen the lamp or otherwise knows of the watch
why: Holmes has said the old man is aware they are interesting themselves in his affairs (¶115), and the lamp is a visible signal. Knowing of the watch is a possibility the story gives reason to consider.

text: Does Dr. Roylott suspect that the room will be watched to-night? — he expects Holmes to interfere but goes ahead regardless
id: q.roylott_suspects=he expects Holmes to interfere but goes ahead regardless
